quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, or on bridges. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: Where is passing prohibited?
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take these steps to drive safely in the dark for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is against the law and very dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is behind you?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Speed up while they are passing.

questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not look at them. Do not speed up or block them, as this can make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When you see a person with a guide dog, white cane, or wheelchair, you must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A person using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device has the right-of-way, whether on a sidewalk or road. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a car to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and force the other car to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two cars reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way. Wait until they pass before you go.

questions.question: When you enter a public road from a driveway or private road, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to cars already on the public road.
Assume other drivers will change lanes for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cars already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering from a driveway or private road, yield to traffic on the public road. Merge safely when you can.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your health does not affect your driving?

options.text: Stay in good physical condition and get regular checkups.
Understand how medicine affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your health affects how well you drive. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Your brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.explanation: You must use a turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey first?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs, signals, and road markings. This includes police officers, fire police, highway workers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has a low clearance. Do not continue if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: Orange signs are used to warn drivers about construction work zones.
questions.explanation: Construction work zones use orange diamond-shaped signs and some rectangular signs. These signs are reflective to help you see them at night.

questions.question: What should concern you most when you see this sign?

options.text: Driving with your headlights out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning, if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or steer sharply. This can make you lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and turn around safely there.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but it harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time, affects your vision, and makes it harder to judge speed and distance. It also makes you take more risks.

questions.question: Your stereo volume should not be so loud that you cannot hear traffic sounds.
questions.explanation: Set your stereo volume before you drive. Lower the volume if you cannot hear normal traffic sounds over the music.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.
The road ahead curves left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will curve to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: When should you drive slower than the posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: You should drive at a safe speed for conditions. This means considering weather, visibility, road condition, and traffic. You must slow down when conditions are unusual.

questions.question: Drivers should keep a safe distance from cyclists.
questions.explanation: You must be careful around cyclists and stay a safe distance away from them.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place a baby or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt a baby or small child, even in a minor crash.
Make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always wear your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce injuries and deaths in crashes. Children 12 and under must sit in the back seat, properly restrained. Never put a rear-facing car seat in the front seat of a car with a front airbag.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, what should you do?

options.text: You can continue or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through.
You must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means that lane does not continue through the interchange. It becomes an exit ramp. If you are in that lane, you can change lanes to continue on the freeway, or you must exit.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, wait until you can see the entire car in your rearview mirror before moving back to the right lane.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle, do not return to your lane until the entire vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Do not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles.

questions.question: When can you drive in a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?

options.text: When you are driving faster than other traffic
When you are driving slower than other traffic
When your vehicle has multiple people in it
When you are in a hurry

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle has multiple people in it
questions.explanation: Some highways have HOV lanes on the left for vehicles with more than one person. These lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the pavement.

questions.question: Use high beam headlights when driving in fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and reduce visibility.

questions.question: What color are warning signs that show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on white background
Black letters or symbols on yellow background
White letters or symbols on blue background
White letters or symbols on green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: Driving ability can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all impair your ability to drive.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is as dangerous as drunk driving. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: Only vehicles with disability plates or placards may park in reserved disability spaces.
questions.explanation: Reserved disability parking spaces can only be used by vehicles displaying disability license plates or disability parking placards.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: You are traveling through an intersection.
You see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, honk if a child runs into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal first, then check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: All people in a moving vehicle must wear a seat belt. Children under age six and those weighing less than 60 pounds must use an approved child car seat.

questions.question: Drivers should be careful when passing large vehicles and avoid driving beside them for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside a large vehicle for long. Either drop back or move ahead to stay safe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must and must not do. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can multiply the effects of both.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can multiply the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs increases how much both affect you. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Create a clear path for the emergency vehicle. If you are in heavy traffic, slow down and move aside when you can.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle while driving?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
Where there is a red light.
When a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer signals you to stop.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, must you yield to drivers who arrived before you?
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: Which describes an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who stares at objects off the road or daydreams.
A driver who looks at a passenger while talking to them.
A driver who only watches the vehicle in front of them.

questions.explanation: Inattentive drivers look at passengers, search for items in the vehicle, read, look at scenery, or daydream instead of watching the road. Stay alert by scanning the road, checking mirrors, and checking your instrument panel regularly.

questions.question: You see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching on a divided multilane highway. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down and move your vehicle to create space for the emergency vehicle. Stop and do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only found in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They show where to position your vehicle, indicate safe passing zones, and warn of upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When stopped by police, what documents must you show?
questions.explanation: You must provide your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. You are required to carry all three documents when driving.

questions.question: What should you do when merging onto a busy freeway?

options.text: Use mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match freeway traffic speed.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Accelerate on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic speed. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging. Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: Must you always obey traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: Yes, they must always be obeyed.
Only when there is other traffic.
Only when a police officer is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and inform drivers of road conditions. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Must you stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful around children.
